question: Which Delhi Sultan appointed people from humble professions to high administrative posts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Tughlaq**, one of the Delhi Sultans, is known for his unorthodox administrative policies and decisions during his reign (1325-1351 CE).
 
• He broke traditional norms and appointed individuals from **humble and low-ranking professions** to high administrative posts.
 
• This policy was driven by his belief in the merit and capability of individuals rather than their social status or birth.
 
• Some of the people appointed to high posts during his reign included **barbers, gardeners, and other individuals from non-aristocratic backgrounds**.
 
• Though innovative, this policy often created resentment among the traditional elite and nobility, leading to unrest and dissatisfaction within the administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Muhammad Tughlaq:**

 
 
• He was the second ruler of the **Tughlaq dynasty** of the Delhi Sultanate and ruled from 1325 to 1351 CE.
 
• He is known for his ambitious projects and administrative reforms, many of which were ahead of their time but failed due to poor execution.
 
• His policies included the **transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad**, introduction of token currency, and tax reforms.
 
 
 
• **Other Delhi Sultans:**
 
 
• **Ruknuddin Firuz:** He ruled for a brief period and is primarily remembered for his weak administration and indulgence in luxury.
 
• **Minhaj-us-Siraj:** He was not a ruler but a historian who documented the history of the Delhi Sultanate in his work, the **Tabqat-i-Nasiri**.
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban:** A strong ruler of the Delhi Sultanate known for his autocratic policies and emphasis on the divine right of kingship.
 
 
 
• **Innovative Policies of Muhammad Tughlaq:**
 
 
• He introduced a system of token currency made of copper and brass to replace gold and silver coins, but this led to rampant counterfeiting.
 
• His decision to shift the capital to Daulatabad aimed to secure the empire from Mongol invasions but caused massive hardships to the population.
 
• He implemented agricultural reforms and increased taxes in the Doab region, but the policy failed due to a famine.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Muhammad Tughlaq:**
 
 
• While his administrative experiments failed, they reflect his visionary and intellectual approach to governance.
 
• He is often referred to as the most **controversial ruler** of the Delhi Sultanate due to his unconventional ideas and policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of Appointing People from Humble Professions:**

 
 
• This policy showcased Muhammad Tughlaq’s belief in **meritocracy** and his willingness to challenge societal norms.
 
• However, it alienated the traditional ruling elite and created friction within the administration.
 
• It also highlights the challenges of implementing progressive policies in a rigidly hierarchical society.
 
 
 
• **Learning from His Reign:**
 
 
• Muhammad Tughlaq’s reign serves as a historical example of the importance of **practical execution** in governance.
 
• His visionary ideas were often undone by his failure to account for the logistical and administrative challenges of implementation.
